clue.text: Wittier men reassembling when it gets cold?

indicators.note: putting the pieces together again in a new arrangement tells us to shuffle the two words before it

explanation.surface: Witty men regroup as the weather turns chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassembling' rearranges the ten letters of WITTIER MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cold season of the year is winter, so a playful description of that season's period.

clue.text: Northern river sport

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England
to sport a badge or hat is to have it on, displaying it

explanation.surface: A northern river associated with a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names the Durham river and also means to display clothing, as in sporting a tie.

clue.text: Grandma eats a sort of bread

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the grandmother word holds the A

parts.note: nan is an informal British word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny tucks into some bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, a type of loaf.

clue.text: One of two I plunged into volatile liquid

indicators.note: plunging into something means going inside it, so I sits within the liquid's word

parts.note: ether is a highly volatile solvent once used as an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dip into a dangerous evaporating fluid, one of a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun picks out one or the other of a pair, either one.

clue.text: Trained athlete is trim, OK? I'm pleased by the improvement!

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach approves as a fit sportsman shapes up nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' looks like it describes the athlete but signals rearranging ATHLETE IS TRIM OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiom of approval said when something gets better.

clue.text: Fellows carrying little girl, coming to a holy city

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so the men word contains the girl

parts.note: fellows are men
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: Men bring a small girl along on a pilgrimage to a sacred city.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia is Islam's second holiest city, burial place of the Prophet.

clue.text: A good journalist over the hill?

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Is a fine reporter past it?
explanation.definitionFit: Being over the hill is an idiom for being past one's prime, that is, old.

clue.text: College people dealing with precious material

definitions.meaning: A college of the University of London
craftsmen who work gold and other precious metals

explanation.surface: A college of dealers in valuable stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names the London college and the craftsmen who make jewellery from gold.

clue.text: Two males interrupting party poem, creating inconvenience

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking in between, so the two males go between party and poem

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
an ode is a lyric poem
M is the abbreviation for male, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: Two men barge into a party's poetry reading and cause a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: To discommode is to put someone out, causing them trouble; the definition is a participial phrase loosely matching the verb.

clue.text: A very great and eccentric bohemian

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of great and are scrambled

explanation.surface: Describing someone as a highly unconventional free spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe unconventional, experimental artistic types, so the adjective is a near-synonym.

clue.text: Palm Sunday's collection for gifts for the poor

indicators.note: a collection of letters drawn from inside the words, running across the start of Palm and the possessive ending

explanation.surface: Money gathered in church on the Sunday before Easter goes to charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' plays on the church offering while picking letters from pALM Sunday'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable donations of money or food to the needy are traditionally called by this word.

clue.text: Troublemaker on a ship, sailor the French blocked

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
SS stands for steamship
AB is an able-bodied seaman
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A rascal aboard ship has the French sailor stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that cannot be travelled because it is obstructed is described this way.

clue.text: International organisation's excellent opening to provide wine?

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, plus the possessive S
topping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: The UN praises a fine start to a drinks reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the cork or stopper from a bottle opens it so the wine can be poured.

clue.text: Country worker gets game bird — not hard

indicators.note: not means leaving out, so the hard letter is dropped from the bird

parts.note: the pheasant is a bird shot for sport
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A farmhand bags a pheasant, though it was an easy shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm labourer or smallholder working the land in rural areas.

clue.text: Breakfast cook who intrudes on another's territory?

definitions.meaning: a pan for cooking eggs gently in simmering water
someone who hunts game illegally on another's land

explanation.surface: A breakfast chef who trespasses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an egg pan and someone who takes game illegally from private land.

clue.text: Given medical care, as discussed

definitions.meaning: a topic dealt with or handled in a talk or essay

explanation.surface: Patients seen to, as already mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The participle means attended by a doctor and also a subject dealt with in writing.

clue.text: Crazy Merton tutor

indicators.note: crazy suggests being jumbled up, so the six letters of the college name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad don at Merton, an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: Merton is an Oxford college, which makes 'tutor' look like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser who guides a student is a close synonym of a teacher.

clue.text: Lordly type will appear in Paris tomorrow

indicators.note: appearing in signals that the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A nobleman is expected in the French capital tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal word for an aristocrat, a person of noble rank.

clue.text: Being opposed to any priest or saint I call 'crime' ridiculously

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests something absurdly mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a holy man by labelling him a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine of hostility to clergy and their influence in public life.

clue.text: Keep quiet in delightful meal

indicators.note: keep tells us one piece holds the other within it
in places the quiet letter inside the delightful word

parts.note: super means delightful or excellent
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Diners are urged to stay silent during a lovely dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening meal, especially a light one, is the standard sense.

clue.text: Come back with vessel for chemistry lab

definitions.meaning: a glass flask with a long bent neck used for distilling

explanation.surface: Returning with lab glassware.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sharp reply and a long-necked distilling flask.

clue.text: Came across house by the end of cobbled way

parts.note: met means came across, encountered

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of the street word

explanation.surface: Found a house at the end of a cobbled street.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a manner or means of doing something, a way.

clue.text: Country team that's taken care of, led by this person

indicators.note: led by puts the person's word in front of the rest

parts.note: this person refers to the setter, me
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
c/o, CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A national side that has been looked after, captained by me.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation in North America.

clue.text: Punished for second parking offence? That's nice!

definitions.meaning: fined again, read playfully as the answer
nice in the sense of cultured, polished or discerning

explanation.surface: A motorist fined a second time hears a sarcastic remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part splits as RE-FINED, fined once more; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in the old sense of fastidious and cultured matches polished manners.

clue.text: Cheese cut short

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word for short loses its final letter

parts.note: brief means short

explanation.surface: A cheese sliced quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese from the region east of Paris.

clue.text: Summer heat is too much for this bird

indicators.note: is too much for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird is overcome by summer temperatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: King entertained by poet and elegist

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in by them, so the king goes inside the poet

parts.note: John Gay was the poet who wrote The Beggar's Opera
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch hosted by a poet who writes laments.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray wrote the famous Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, making him an elegist.

clue.text: Oh, the crime can be so alluring!

indicators.note: can be so hints the letters might take another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over how tempting wrongdoing can be.
explanation.definitionFit: An inviting, flirtatious look beckons someone closer, so seductive or enticing.

clue.text: So there is an attempt after a bit of hesitation

indicators.note: after places the attempt word behind the hesitation sound

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates briefly and then has a try.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin connective meaning therefore, used to draw a conclusion.

clue.text: A railway needs to go east of somewhere like Paddington still

indicators.note: in an across answer east means to the right, so the following pieces come after the place

parts.note: Paddington is a major railway station in London

explanation.surface: A railway line must head east of a London terminus that is stalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Not moving at all, motionless, is the adjective's meaning.
